newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar heads lower, spread holds at $5.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar heads lower, spread holds at $5.

text.p: London's nearby August white sugar contract slid below $320 in solid early volume on Monday but scale-down buying from commission houses dragged the contract off its $319.30 low.

Market sources said mixed selling on August, including some from trade players, accounted for the bulk of the turnover. But this was also boosted by some crosses and August/October spread trades, they said.
"There's good volume although there are some crosses," said one trader.
While still on the narrow side, August/October managed to hold above $5.00 as broker selling failed to push October through support at $314.

At 1135 GMT August was $1.70 lower at $319.50 and October down 90 cents at $314.40. Volume amounted to 708 lots, more than half of which was in August, which traders said was an encouraging sign of liquidity.
Technical analysts said August's recent weakness could be a sign of a market reversal.
"The short-term picture is starting to worry us for the failure to break through $325 suggests a possible short-term reversal," said Adrian Haylor, a technical analyst at Sucden.

While the market was currently supported around $320, if prices were to close below that point then $315 could soon be tested, he said, adding that the outlook would improve if $325 resistance were broken.
Fresh fundamental news was thin on the ground.

The Thai Cane Sugar Board said 1997/98 sugar output could fall by 10 percent due to a lack of rainfall, bringing production to around 5.0-5.2 million tonnes from around 5.7 million tonnes (tel quel) this year.
All traded contracts were also lower in Paris where volume totalled 262 lots. August was down 70 cents at $319.60 and October down 80 at $314.00.
